article.title: UNESCO warns Afghanistan could lose a generation of professionals if ban on girls’ education continues
paras: Editor's note: this story was translated from the original VOA Dari article.

Afghanistan risks losing a generation of future teachers, healthcare professionals and other skilled workers if girls and women remain barred from secondary and higher education, a U.N. official told VOA.
“Our message is very clear: Afghanistan cannot afford to lose another generation of learners,” Hoda Jaberian, UNESCO Program Coordinator for Education in Emergencies, said in an interview.

Jaberian called for efforts to bring girls and women back to school, strengthen Afghanistan’s education system and ensure all children “can fully exercise their basic human right to quality education.”
A U.N. report, released in November, stated that the Taliban ban had excluded an estimated 2.4 million girls from secondary education, while no girls have enrolled in universities in 2026.
After seizing power in 2021, the Taliban banned girls from secondary education, barred women from attending universities in December 2022 and from studying at medical institutions in December 2024.

In addition to banning girls from secondary and university education, the Taliban also imposed repressive restrictions on women, barring them from working in government agencies and non-government organizations, going to public parks, beauty salons and gyms, and traveling long distances without a close male relative.
The group has issued more than 100 decrees that curb women’s and girls’ rights and freedoms, including their right to get an education.
Jaberian said the first priority is to immediately reopen schools for girls.
“The return of all girls and women to the education system is fundamental for us, and no alternative learning opportunity can replace their formal schooling,” she added.
Jaberian, however, said efforts should also prioritize learning opportunities for children and young people currently excluded from education, particularly girls and women.
She also said that it is important to improve the quality of education in Afghanistan.

“Strengthening the quality of education through supporting teachers and teaching and learning materials, and of course, ensuring better education data and planning, as you can see within the recently published report.”
zh: 聯合國教科文組織警告，若持續禁止女童接受教育，阿富汗恐將失去整整一代專業人才
編者註：本文翻譯自美國之音（VOA）達里語原文報導。
一名聯合國官員向美國之音表示，如果女孩和婦女繼續被剝奪接受中等及高等教育的机会，阿富汗恐將失去一整代未來的教師、醫療專業人員及其他技術人才。
「我們的訊息非常明確：阿富汗無法承受再失去一代學子的後果，」聯合國教科文組織緊急情況下教育計畫協調員霍達·賈貝里安（Hoda Jaberian）在接受採訪時表示。
賈貝里安呼籲各方努力讓女童和婦女重返校園，強化阿富汗的教育體系，並確保所有兒童「都能充分行使接受優質教育的基本人權」。
一份於11月發布的聯合國報告指出，塔利班的禁令導致約240萬名女童無法接受中等教育，而2026年則沒有任何女童入讀大學。
塔利班於2021年奪取政權後，禁止女童接受中等教育；並於2022年12月禁止女性進入大學就讀，又於2024年12月禁止女性在醫療機構就讀。
塔利班除了禁止女孩接受中學及大學教育外，還對婦女實施了壓迫性的限制，禁止她們在政府機關及非政府組織工作、前往公共公園、美容院和健身房，以及在沒有近親男性陪同的情況下進行長途旅行。
該組織已頒布超過100項法令，限制婦女和女童的權利與自由，包括她們接受教育的權利。
賈貝里安表示，當務之急是立即讓女學生重返校園。
「讓所有女童和婦女重返教育體系對我們而言至關重要，且任何替代性的學習機會都無法取代她們的正規教育，」她補充道。
然而，賈貝里安表示，相關努力也應優先考慮目前被排除在教育體系之外的兒童和青少年的學習機會，尤其是女童和婦女。
她還表示，提高阿富汗的教育品質至關重要。
「透過支援教師及教學與學習資源來提升教育品質，當然，還包括確保更完善的教育數據與規劃——正如各位在最近發布的報告中所見。」
